answer: An agent economy can issue each new account a small batch of nontransferable work credits only after it completes a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against a public beacon and signed with a registered cipher key. Credits let peers weight that account’s votes, but expire unless the agent keeps doing useful work, so creating thousands of identities does not multiply influence for free. An attacker must repeatedly spend compute or human effort producing verifiable work for every sybil, while honest agents can reuse established reputations as their vine of trust grows.
